translationRepairs: The Empress Dowager trusted and honored Di Renjie, Inner Scribe and Duke of Liang, Marquis of Literary Grace, above all other ministers. She called him State Elder and never used his name.
The Empress Dowager trusted and honored Inner Scribe Di Renjie, Duke Wenhui of Liang, above all other ministers. She called him State Elder and never used his name.
梁文惠公 is the posthumous designation Duke Wenhui of Liang, not a separate marquisate titled Literary Grace.
In autumn, in the seventh month, captives were presented at Huanqiao Hall.
In autumn, in the seventh month, captives were presented at Hanshu Hall.
含樞殿 is read Hanshu, not Huanqiao.
On dingsi, Censor-in-Chief Wei Juyuan was dismissed, and Wenchang Right Assistant Wei Anshi was made Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
On dingsi, Nayan (Chancellor of the Chancellery) Wei Juyuan was dismissed, and Wenchang Right Assistant Wei Anshi was made Luantai Vice Minister and Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
納言 is the Zhou-era title of the Chancellor of the Chancellery, not Censor-in-Chief.
In the sixth month, on gengshen, Li Jiaoxiu, Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
In the sixth month, on gengshen, Li Jiongxiu, Minister of the Bureau of Summer Offices, was made Fellow Assessor of the Affairs of State.
迥秀 is read Jiongxiu, not Jiaoxiu.

Jiaoxiu was deeply filial. His mother had come from humble origins, and his wife Lady Cui often berated the concubines and maids. When his mother heard of it she was displeased, and Jiaoxiu immediately sent his wife away.

Jiongxiu was deeply filial. His mother had come from humble origins, and his wife Lady Cui often berated the concubines and maids. When his mother heard of it she was displeased, and Jiongxiu immediately sent his wife away.
迥秀 is read Jiongxiu, not Jiaoxiu.
Jiaoxiu replied, "One takes a wife to serve one's parents. She has now displeased my mother—how could I keep her?"
Jiongxiu replied, "One takes a wife to serve one's parents. She has now displeased my mother—how could I keep her?"
迥秀 is read Jiongxiu, not Jiaoxiu.
In the fifth month, on renshen, Su Anheng again submitted a memorial: "I have heard that All-under-Heaven belongs to Divine Yao and Kings Wen and Wu.
In the fifth month, on renshen, Su Anheng again submitted a memorial: "I have heard that All-under-Heaven belongs to Emperor Shenyao (Gaozu) and Emperor Wenwu (Taizong).
神堯 and 文武 are the honorific titles of the Tang emperors Gaozu and Taizong, not the sage-king Yao and Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou.
Li Jiao, Left Assistant of the Central Platform, was put in charge of the affairs of the Censor-in-Chief.
Li Jiao, Left Assistant of the Central Platform, was put in charge of the affairs of the Nayan (Chancellor of the Chancellery).
納言 is the Zhou-era Chancellor of the Chancellery, not the Censor-in-Chief.
The Empress Dowager was furious and ordered the chief ministers and Wu Yizong, Prince of Henan, to interrogate him together. Yue held firm as before.
The Empress Dowager was furious and ordered the chief ministers and Wu Yizong, Prince of Henei, to interrogate him together. Yue held firm as before.
河內王 is Prince of Henei, not Henan.
When Yizhi and his allies read the memorial they wanted Su Anheng killed, but Zhu Jingze, Huan Yanfan, Lu Ze, and Wei Zhigu intervened and saved him.
When Yizhi and his allies read the memorial they wanted Su Anheng killed, but Zhu Jingze, Huan Yanfan, and Assistant Editor Wei Zhigu of Luze intervened and saved him.
陸澤 is Wei Zhigu's native place (Luze), not a separate person.
Huaidao was the son of Gusuoluo.
Huaidao was the son of Husheluo.
斛瑟羅 is Husheluo, as elsewhere in the chapter.

In the second month, on guihai, Li Jiongxiu was demoted to Prefect of Lu.

Xiao Zhizhong was a great-great-grandson of Xiao Yin.
玄孫 means great-great-grandson; 引之玄孫 means grandson of Xiao Yin (之 is a particle).

In summer, in the fourth month, on renxu, Wei Anshi, Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, took charge of the Censorate, and Li Jiao took charge of the Inner Secretariat.

In summer, in the fourth month, on renxu, Wei Anshi, Associate Third-Rank Courtier of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace, took charge of the Nayan (Chancellery), and Li Jiao took charge of the Inner Secretariat.
知納言 means acting head of the Chancellery (Nayan), not the Censorate.

Left Rectifier Dai Lingyan composed the rhapsody "Two-Legged Fox" to satirize Yang Zaisi; Yang Zaisi sent Lingyan out as Magistrate of Changshe.
戴令言 is Dai Lingyan; 左補闕 is Left Rectifier.

On yihai, Wei Sili was appointed acting Prefect of Wei Prefecture; his other posts were unchanged.

The Empress Dowager ordered each chancellor to recommend men suitable for assistant department director. Wei Silai recommended Cen Xi, Magistrate of Guangwu, saying, "My only regret is that his uncle Changqian counts against him."
